name: Bean Burrito

ingredients.name: cooked pinto or black beans, drained
red and yellow bell peppers, diced
vegetarian melting cheese made with vegetarian coagulants, grated

steps: Drain the cooked beans well. Heat 10 ml oil in a wide pan, cook the onion and diced peppers for 5–6 minutes until just softened, then stir in cumin and chilli powder for 30 seconds. Add the beans and half the salt; cook 3–4 minutes, lightly mashing a quarter of the beans so the filling holds together. Keep the mixture moist but not watery.

Warm the cooked rice with the remaining salt, lime juice and half the chopped coriander. Warm the thick salsa separately if desired. Check the cheese label to ensure it contains no animal-derived coagulants. Set out four large tortillas, the beans, rice, peppers, salsa and grated cheese before assembling.

Warm each tortilla briefly in a dry pan, 15–20 seconds per side, until flexible. Place one-quarter of the rice in a short strip just below the centre, then add one-quarter of the bean-pepper mixture, 30 g salsa, 30 g cheese and a little of the remaining coriander. Leave generous empty space at both sides and do not overfill.

Fold the short sides inward over the filling. Lift the bottom edge over it, tuck firmly, and roll away from you into a tight, fully closed cylinder. Repeat for all four burritos, placing each seam-side down. If a tortilla cracks, warm it a little longer before rolling.

Heat the remaining 5 ml oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Toast the burritos seam-side down for 2–3 minutes, turn and toast the other side for 2 minutes, until lightly browned and the cheese melts. Rest for 2 minutes and cut diagonally; serve with any extra salsa and lime.
tips: Use cooked beans and cooked rice; raw weights would require different cooking times. The reviewed photo shows sliced toasted burritos with distinct beans, rice, peppers, tomato and cheese. Keep salsa thick so the tortilla does not become soggy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
